methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series G → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.25x) to $500M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Robotics & Manufacturing (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Robotics & Manufacturing, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Wandelbots is a Series G robotics and manufacturing software company founded by Christian Piechnick that has raised $126M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of nine private peers (including Divergent, Exotec, and Locus Robotics) and one public comparable, though narrow peer overlap at this stage and valuation tier limits direct multiples-based triangulation.

Stage-progression methodology applies here, using total capital raised as a proxy baseline of $500M and applying a 1.25x step-up multiplier typical for Series G advancement. This yields an implied valuation of $625M. Peer-median analysis was not applicable; while 11 robotics and manufacturing companies exist in the reference set, no subset of three or more comps matched the target's stage, tier, and valuation concurrently, making a narrow peer median unreliable without risking distortion from broader sector comparables.

The triangulation supports a valuation range of $531M (low) to $719M (high), with a median of $625M. This single-method result carries execution risk: the stage-progression approach relies on the $500M baseline as a proxy rather than observed market pricing. Key uncertainties include the target's unit economics trajectory, customer concentration, and competitive positioning within the rapidly evolving robotics stack—factors not fully captured by stage-based mechanics alone. Additional data on recent financials or customer retention would materially narrow confidence intervals.
